# Bounded Migration operator runbook

Current scope (2026-11-13): TokenStaking remains in scope because its backing
was migrated to the old DTF DETF. Plain DTF holdings use ordinary new deposits.
E-S is admitted through the fixed held-SE/LP path below; historical proof
sections retain their narrower coverage at the time of those runs.

## Bounded deployment and interrupted preparation

The registered Migration package now requires `prepareSyChildren(fullArgs)`
before `deployVault(fullArgs)`. Preparation constructs the bound, unreserved
bond and both empty SY children; the final transaction creates and publishes
the complete parent. Both operations use identical full arguments, including
the actual hook. The `deploy` CLI stage performs them in dependency order.

Deployment simulation, estimation, signing and resumed intents are constrained
to 32,000,000 gas per transaction. A larger Anvil block limit is not a larger
permitted deployment envelope. Preparation reconciliation independently hashes
the full arguments, checks the package's completed construction record,
authenticates its child arguments and registry/factory identities, and verifies
the absent parent/receipt and inert children at the preparation receipt block.
The SY package ABI must be included as the fingerprinted `sy-package-abi` source.

After a crash following mined preparation, `resume` remains read-only unless
execution is explicitly selected. Executing resume authenticates the same
canonical preparation receipt and child identities, then submits only the
remaining final transaction. Do not discard the signed journal and replay
preparation against an already constructed parent.

## Delegated-wallet claim authentication

A member may include `execution: { kind: "direct-eip7702-v1", delegate,
delegateCodeHash }` when the original wallet directly signs the source claim.
The original wallet remains the signed sender, source caller, SY recipient
and eventual bond beneficiary. Authenticate stable pre/post delegation code
and delegate runtime, exactly one source invocation, and no execution of the
claimant's wallet code within that source transaction. All existing source,
canonical-block, measured-unit and complete-original checks still apply.

For a signed outer transaction addressed to the original delegated wallet,
`relayed-eip7702-v1` separates the outer signer from the actual source caller.
The canonical successful trace must contain exactly one fixed-source claim
from the original wallet, with its exact input, return, nested vault redemption,
source events and measured weight/share/SY deltas. Failed inner calls and
ambiguous multiple-source calls are rejected even if the outer receipt succeeds.
The observed delegate hash binds runtime identity; it does not grant the
relayer a Migration role or infer a wallet authorization policy.

This does not admit the historical indirect EntryPoint transaction or remove
the isolated-block requirement. A delegated wallet must also accept the real
funded bond's ERC721 callback; rejection rolls back Migration custody and
issuance. The original wallet remains the bond beneficiary.

## Conserved TokenStaking remainder

The owner selected one economic original across eligible remaining claims and
already-claimed SY, excluding disposed or previously compensated portions.
The bounded `complete-remaining-token-staking` certificate keeps the full
original ETH/DTF contributions, adds `review.originalWeight`, and retains
`review.eligibleWeight`. Both weights use native18 parent units; the
configured `originalUnits` is the measured native9 SY representing the
complete eligible remainder. These units are not interchangeable.

Preparation authenticates every admitted source claim and requires its
consumed-weight sum to equal the complete eligible remainder. Original weight,
eligibility and exclusions are reviewed inputs, not inferred from current
balances. Existing direct signed EOA, canonical isolated-block, source-runtime,
measured-output, unrelated-budget and anti-downgrade checks remain in force.
The original identity cannot simultaneously appear as ordinary SY or another
compensated representation. Prior delivered Migration credit remains excluded
from this bounded intake.

The complete measured SY balance and excluded floor are authenticated at the
pinned preparation block. A later holder transfer does not erase the configured
original or block the owner's paid first bond and activation. Current asset
control is enforced by the actual surrender transaction: missing assets revert
without custody or credit changes, and returning them to the original wallet
does not require reconstructing intermediate transfers.

The operator uses `configureClaimedSyEntitlements` and preserves both the full
original quote and `floor(originalCredit * eligibleWeight / originalWeight)`.
It rejects an absent/invalid denominator or zero remaining credit, binds the
weight basis in the configuration hash, and verifies `claimedSyWeights`.
Do not multiply down ETH/DTF quantities and quote them again. Later partial
SY surrender consumes the stored remaining credit proportionally, with final
rounding residue paid only when the remainder is surrendered.

This path requires complete preparation of the configured eligible remainder
before Stage 1 loading; it does not add a raw-weight pull or authenticate a
delegated wallet. Source claims themselves issue no compensation. A later
Migration failure restores its SY custody and credit, not earlier completed
source claims. The original complete-original certificate remains supported.

## Separate NFT contribution bonds

Set `separateContributions: true` on the reviewed NFT `original` record to
configure two bonds, with ETH first and DTF second. Both original amounts must
be positive. Omit the field for the existing single-bond mode. The proof binds
the mode together with the full original; changing or removing it requires a
reviewed replacement, not an operator-only switch.

For weighted collection `0xfe4cc6d5faafdf210af4e728f4108fcaad9bb65e`, ID `3`,
the owner selected separate originals of `999999000000000` raw18 WETH and
`362893857600000000000` raw18 DTF. Preparation quotes each against the same
frozen snapshot and records both credits. The configure stage selects
`configureNftContributionEntitlements`; the typed Forge helper is
`configureNftContributions`. Its configuration hash includes the separate-mode
boolean, so resume verification cannot confuse it with a single-bond record.

One eligible Stage 2 whole-NFT surrender creates both bonds atomically. The
legacy scalar return reports the first bond ID and total delivered credit;
read `nftContributionSurrenders` or the per-contribution events for both IDs
and principals. Each stored credit is scaled by remaining principal separately.
This is not an independent compensation allocation. Configuration still
requires reviewed source units, wallet identity and non-overlapping exposure.

## Finite conversion and recovery receipt selection

Add `--selection conversions-and-recoveries` to `collect-receipts` to select
every authenticated row in `conversions.csv` and `observed-recoveries.csv`.
Omitting selection preserves the existing purchase/claim collector. No execution
command accepts selection. The same five read methods, provider, anchor, exclusive
output and safe raw capture rules below apply. Do not replay the old purchase
archive separately. Counts and request hashes derive from complete bound rows.

Every selected row retains its original fields and logical locator. Recovery
matching requires exact transaction, log index, asset, recipient, integer amount
and declared block. Conversion matching requires exact output asset, recipient,
amount and declared block; zero/multiple matches and shared transactions stay
explicit. Blank amounts stay unknown, never zero. Candidate transfers and exact
matches are retained individually, never allocated transaction totals.

These are reviewed observations only. Keep token/native units separate. Labels
such as `is_external_recovery=false`, `deduct_from_R=false` or blank `R_eth`
are historical fields, not proof of zero compensation or approved deductions.
Matching gross output is not net contribution, current control, transferred
entitlement, principal/reward attribution, W0/Q0 or source admission. This
selection does not relax direct-EOA claim admission. The NON-ISSUABLE archive
remains rejected by operational intake and does not close old candidate unknowns.

## Finite named receipt evidence

```sh
bun scripts/recovery/dtf-migration/cli.ts collect-receipts \
  --input "$COMPLETE_HISTORICAL_TREE" --output "$NEW_RECEIPT_DIRECTORY" \
  --rpc-alias robinhood_mainnet_alchemy
```

Use the existing login-shell archive credential bootstrap. The command reads
only `ALCHEMY_KEY` and the configured alias in `foundry.toml`; never place an
endpoint or credential in argv. There is no endpoint override, signer,
automatic retry, provider fallback or installation. Invalid historical bindings
fail before RPC configuration is read. Offline tests use a local wire server;
the live CLI accepts only the existing Robinhood Alchemy alias.

All manifest/source raw bindings authenticate before deriving the complete
S008 weighted purchases, S009 earlier CP purchases, and `legacy_weight_to_sy`
conversion references. Every original row is retained. Duplicate transaction
hashes share requests, not economic attribution. The observed full historical
population is 43 weighted, 16 earlier and 18 raw claims (77 distinct hashes);
these counts are derived, not a hardcoded request list.

Before named collection, authenticate chain 4663 and canonical block 108944663,
hash `0xc497433dd691a40cb85959cfeba2e3fff85a975ae060612d984998e1d5765733`.
Only `eth_chainId`, `eth_getTransactionByHash`, `eth_getTransactionReceipt`,
`eth_getBlockByHash`, and `eth_getBlockByNumber` are sent. Each distinct named
transaction and receipt is requested once. Exact blocks are cached by hash and
number, without range scans. A failed request stays failed; unaffected finite
requests continue. Wrong chain/anchor stops named requests and accounts for
every reference as unavailable. Provider refusal is evidence, never permission
to switch providers, methods, scan ranges or trace execution.

`http/` preserves request bytes and complete safe response entity bytes (not
HTTP framing or original signed transactions). `http-manifest.json` binds byte
lengths, SHA-256, request IDs/methods/parameters, HTTP status and response outcome.
Credential-bearing responses are sanitized, named `.response.redacted`, marked
`raw: false`, and rejected as successful observations. Transport failures retain
sanitized error details, never an endpoint-bearing exception. `archive.json`
records normalized successes, partial failures, canonical associations and exact
request links. `references.json` retains source rows and request deduplication;
`reconciliation.json` accounts for every reference, conflict and qualification.
Output creation and every file write are exclusive. Preserve any partial output
and command failure; never reuse an output directory.

Transaction/receipt/block identities, index membership, receipt endpoints,
every log identity/order, canonical block agreement, successful receipt status
and the anchor upper bound are checked. Purchase reconciliation requires both
the exact NFT mint/recipient and its generation-specific purchase event/basis.
Direct DTF/WETH and routed inputs stay separate. Shared/multiaction or indirect
purchases never attribute the whole transaction input to each original.
Claim reconciliation retains caller/callee/value/calldata, source/SY logs and
exact known output locators/amounts. Only a direct exact-length call to the fixed
TokenStaking address is decoded as `withdrawClaim`; arbitrary calldata is not.
Event signatures/layouts are local interface interpretation, not authenticated
historical build provenance.

The archive version is `dtf-finite-receipt-evidence-v1`, status
`NON-ISSUABLE-RECEIPT-OBSERVATIONS`; operational loaders reject it. Gross transfers,
mints and matching events do not establish net contribution or eligibility.
This is observed RPC JSON, not a trustless proof, historical storage, execution
prefix, current control, full W0/Q0, all prior claims or zero prior compensation.
It does not modify candidates or close all 1240 unresolved records, exhaustive
native/WETH/refund/recovery/source exposure, configuration, funding, C0 or credit.
Preserve recovered-input qualification and all source/external/gas/P1 limits.

## Offline historical review candidates

```sh
bun scripts/recovery/dtf-migration/cli.ts derive-candidates \
  --input "$COMPLETE_HISTORICAL_TREE" --output "$NEW_CANDIDATE_DIRECTORY"
```

The input directory contains the original `manifest.json`, `sources.json` and
every declared file. Preserve relative paths, including the pre-exploit sibling.
Supply paths explicitly; there is no default workstation path, network lookup,
RPC, signer or acquisition fallback. Every declared byte length and SHA-256,
including Markdown, must match before any raw CSV is parsed. The manifest is
the explicit trust root; its binding authenticates `sources.json` before that
index is parsed. Missing, altered or symlinked inputs reject. A supplied
hash-authenticated recovered historical body is not an original capture:
retain its recovery provenance separately, never change a binding to accept
later annotations. The annotated primary tree remains a negative case.

`candidates.json` has version `dtf-historical-review-candidates-v1` and status
`NON-ISSUABLE-REVIEW-CANDIDATES`. It is rejected by preparation, prepared-manifest
validation and execution schemas. It supplies no configuration IDs, C0,
approved flags, invented economic origins, Q0 or known-zero prior credit.
Existing `prepare`/`validate`/execution and journal semantics are unchanged.
Only the new offline command accepts this historical tree.

The weighted NFT join uses S008 purchases, S011 mint/input transfers and S006
pre-incident DTF details, retaining chain/collection/ID, recipient/payer,
purchase/mint/input locators and separate observed DTF/WETH. Transaction sharing,
mint and payer conflicts prohibit unique input attribution. An observed zero
means zero in the saved inbound subset, not zero native cost, refund or net
contribution. The 41 pre-incident and two later purchases are observations, not
eligibility decisions. S009 retains all earlier LP-accounting-lock observations,
direct DTF/WETH and routed intermediate DTF separately. Its unavailable original
raw receipts remain a qualification; routed DTF is not another contribution.

The complete CSV census retains original fields as `historicalFields` alongside
parsed integer/unknown quantities and review links. Blank quantities become
null; only the original signed `gons_delta` column accepts negative integers.
LP-accounting shares, physical LP, gons, raw weights and native9/18/19/28 remain
distinct. No sums across those units are produced. Position/exclusion,
account/position/holding/recovery/exception, index-subset, NFT funding/claim
and observed-output relations are checked. Machine-readable unresolved records
identify missing basis, aliases, previous delivery, incomplete receipts/native/
WETH/recoveries, stale control and unobserved accepted categories. Historical
look-through/held totals are diagnostics, never Q0, contribution inputs or awards.
Unrecomputed reported fields are listed explicitly, not accepted as proven.

All historical policy fields are retained only as history. Current plan r5 and
PRD r22 govern, especially MIG-R42 configured original-wallet/control and
Stage2-only surrender. Old bearer, loss-formula, no-credit-after-custody and
upfront-zero wording supplies no authority. Do not require intermediate-holder
ancestry as a surrender prerequisite. Independent recipient observations remain
separate from asset-surrender candidates; both need disjoint-original review.
Standalone native/WETH observations are contribution/recovery provenance, not
new compensated surrender routes.

Writes are exclusive to a new output directory. Retain every failed output and
command. Repeated runs and a complete byte-preserving relocation from another
CWD produce identical canonical bytes. No wall clock or absolute input paths
enter candidates. To verify the new source boundary locally:

```sh
bun node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit --target ES2022 --module ESNext \
  --moduleResolution Bundler --strict --noUncheckedIndexedAccess \
  --exactOptionalPropertyTypes --verbatimModuleSyntax --skipLibCheck \
  --types node scripts/recovery/dtf-migration/*.ts
bun test --timeout 15000 ./scripts/recovery/dtf-migration/*.test.ts
```

Before any live preparation, separately acquire missing original data/receipts,
refresh pinned current control and recoveries, reconcile exact original units
and contribution components, remaining rights, aliases and previous delivery,
independently review disjoint values, then arrange actual funding and capture
the supported immutable mint-preview snapshot. Only separately reviewed
originals may enter the existing loader preparation. This command does not
close E-S, broader TokenStaking conservation, disabled conversions, operational
dataset approval, selected reserve composition, deployment gas or missing P1
historical artifacts, and does not authorize acquisition or public execution.

## Saved-evidence bundles and fresh relocation

Every rehearsal requires `--bundle "$AUTHORITY_BUNDLE"`, naming a supplied
complete authority bundle's `bundle.json`. There is no default host inventory
or old-worktree fallback. A strict `dtf-operator-authorities-v1` export input
supplies all 22 distinct `authorityRoles` in `bundle.ts`, with original raw
SHA-256, byte length and provenance. Preserve every source qualification.
Runtime acquisition records and four actual ABI artifacts are additional
bound inputs, not substitutes for those authorities.

```sh
bun scripts/recovery/dtf-migration/cli.ts bundle-export \
  --input "$NATIVE_INPUT" --output "$NEW_BUNDLE_DIRECTORY"
bun scripts/recovery/dtf-migration/cli.ts bundle-materialize \
  --input "$BUNDLE_MANIFEST" --output "$NEW_MATERIALIZATION_DIRECTORY"
```

Export accepts a native authority input, preparation input, prepared manifest
or execution manifest. Its raw template, explicitly referenced sources,
snapshot ABI and bound prepared manifest are saved without changing bytes.
Nothing else is discovered or downloaded. Do not include secrets, environment
files or keystores in source lists. Export is offline integrity/transport,
not chain authentication or historical eligibility. Duplicate/conflicting
source identities, ambiguous references and missing inputs reject.

Copy the complete bundle directory to another owned data root, then materialize.
The loader reads every declared regular file, checks raw hash/byte length,
requires exact data membership and rejects traversal and symlinks, including
symlinked roots/ancestors. Original paths are metadata lookup keys, never
alternate filesystem locations. Missing or changed data fails while the old
host file still exists. Do not merge partial exports.

Materialization creates new local templates/manifests, not original captures.
Preparation retains live canonical verification. Post-capture execution
materialization rebuilds preparation against the actual chain and compares
all original saved payloads, configuration IDs, quotes and dispositions.
Prepare and execution revalidate their complete bound bundle. Native absolute
inputs and their existing hash/domain rules remain supported.

Two locations on the same chain/snapshot/originals must produce identical
onchain payload bytes, configuration IDs and frozen quotes. Normalized hashes
and execution domains intentionally differ: locations remain hashed.
Use fresh preparation and checkpoints after relocation. Never migrate an
already signed journal; changed-domain resume rejects. Each genuine resume
uses unchanged inputs in one location. Full replacements and new harvest
selections use fresh templates/domains, not edits to prior bundles/journals.

The complete portable workflow uses only owned loopback18575:

```sh
bun scripts/recovery/dtf-migration/cli.ts rehearse \
  --bundle "$AUTHORITY_BUNDLE" \
  --rpc-alias robinhood_mainnet_alchemy --fork-block 108944663 --port 18575 \
  --checkpoint .omo-runtime/dtf-migration-portable/checkpoints \
  --evidence docs/incidents/2026-09-16-dtf-recovery/migration/portable-operator/implementation/runtime
```

Forge/Anvil resolve from `PATH` or explicit `FORGE_BIN`/`ANVIL_BIN` executables.
Select a Solar-capable installation; no install or compiler fallback occurs.
Installed source, dependencies and Foundry artifacts are prerequisites.
The existing login-shell archive bootstrap remains; never print its resolved
credential URL. Same-host relocation is not cold dependency reconstruction or
cross-platform proof. P1's two historical artifact JSON versions remain
unrecovered. Operational originals, source limits and target gas stay open.

## Complete-original TokenStaking claims prepared into SY

This intake admits only a reviewed original whose entire eligible native18
weight W0 was consumed by direct signed EOA `withdrawClaim` operations before
its Stage1 loading. The source is fixed to chain4663 TokenStaking
`0xe4c9ff4cfd17ae73ecb3825ebdf7db113c146d00`, Wrapped phase2, claim vault
`0xaf5c0cd3fdedd10bee00eff77fa0429bacdb41f0`, and native9 SY
`0xb55604cf4dcdabb362078e106d20f98512391edf`. Vault shares are native19.
This is prior holder preparation, not an approved Migration pull of raw weight.

Add `claimedOrigin` to the existing `weightedSy` row. Its typed schema is
`claimedSyCertificate` in the existing operator schema. Keep the canonical
wallet-independent `originalId`, original wallet and complete known E0/D0.
The reviewed record explicitly supplies positive `eligibleWeight`, known
`priorDeliveredCredit: "0"`, principal-only eligibility, reward exclusions,
reconciled aliases, no competing representation, and unrelated weight/SY
floors. Unknown or nonzero prior delivery, incomplete original components,
partial preparation and aggregate zero SY are rejected. No allocation here
approves operational historical records.

Each member contains original raw signed bytes, transaction/block identities,
positive native18 `consumedWeight`, exact native9 `receivedSy`, and measured
native19 `redeemedVaultShares`. The admitted execution form is a direct
code-less EOA transaction in an isolated canonical block. Contract wallets,
delegation, special execution and multi-transaction preparation blocks are
not admitted by this validator. A different form needs source admission,
not a guessed trace interpretation.

Preparation checks exact `sum(consumedWeight) == W0` and positive
`Q0 = sum(receivedSy)`, including every actually committed zero-output slice.
Set `originalUnits = Q0`. Never use total wallet balance, an old weight/SY
ratio, a scaled nonlinear input, or a separate full quote for each split.
The existing frozen evaluator quotes complete E0/D0 once; partial and terminal
SY surrender use the existing remaining-Q/C arithmetic unchanged.

The row's `proof` points at the entire reviewed
`{ original, claimedOrigin }` object, not its `original` child. A stripped
certificate therefore cannot validate against that same evidence as ordinary
SY. `claimedSyEvidenceId(domain, original, certificate)` computes the required
nonzero commitment, excluding only the commitment's own field. It binds chain,
Migration proxy, frozen snapshot, complete original inputs, review and every
member. The ordinary-independent SY proof form remains unchanged.
Classification is also reconciled across all referenced reviewed JSON
documents. Selecting a nested or separately copied original tuple does not
erase a claimed-origin marker elsewhere in those reviewed records.
The certificate also binds the actual `snapshotCapture` transaction, RPC
block number and block hash. Its successful canonical receipt must contain
the parent's matching `MigrationSnapshotCaptured` event. The event's EVM
`block.number` is not substituted for the RPC height: those differ on the
admitted Robinhood fork.

The actual RPC, not an uploaded receipt, authenticates canonical block/receipt/
transaction identity, signed caller and calldata, return and claim event,
same-wallet vault redemption, source phase/asset/decimals and admitted proxy/
facet runtimes. Historical source weight/supply/vault/SY deltas must match
the exact member quantities. Unique transactions cannot appear twice within
or across originals. Historical and current aggregate wallet budgets protect
measured descendants and unrelated SY; current consumed units come only from
the real Migration record. Current control at surrender remains mandatory.
Previously configured SY origins must remain in the complete manifest census,
including on subsequent preparation, execution and resume.

Reviewed owner inputs establish historical eligibility, original contributions,
known-zero prior delivery and semantic origin disjointness. Chain observations
establish execution and quantities, not those historical facts. An opaque alias
still requires owner reconciliation. The unchanged onchain loader trusts owner
loading and the evidence commitment; it does not independently authenticate
offchain certificates. Its canonical origin guards exclude other backed,
receipt, liquid, SY, vault-share, LP, NFT and independent representations.
Configuration and resume reconstruct and reauthenticate the prepared manifest
before any signing, so changed evidence, domain or payload cannot be adopted.

The new cumulative rehearsal is:

```sh
/bin/zsh -lc 'bun scripts/recovery/dtf-migration/cli.ts rehearse \
  --bundle "$AUTHORITY_BUNDLE" \
  --rpc-alias robinhood_mainnet_alchemy --fork-block 108944663 --port 18573 \
  --checkpoint .omo-runtime/dtf-migration-claimed-sy/checkpoints \
  --evidence docs/incidents/2026-09-16-dtf-recovery/migration/claimed-sy-integration/implementation/runtime'
```

All earlier loopback gates/routes and three genuine mined-before-checkpoint
resumes remain. The new full/split originals use controlled direct signatures,
actual donor reassignments, real gas transfers and positive excluded weight/SY
floors. Donor impersonation and synthetic historical partitions are labeled
separately. Lossless raw input captures distinguish original bytes from JSON
serialization or later reconstruction. No gas/code/storage/token injection,
source governance or public operation is needed.

Stage1 still rejects surrender. The paid owner-first bond precedes permanent
loader removal and Stage2 opening. Each successful same-wallet SY surrender
creates an exactly funded fresh90-day bond. A later child-funding failure
restores that later SY/Migration transaction, not the earlier source claim:
consumed raw weight stays consumed and the prepared SY stays with its wallet.
Unchanged ordinary-SY contract-receiver/reentry tests are shared-path coverage,
not claimed-origin callback witnesses. EOA-only admission is not broadened.

Direct raw pull, partial/prior-delivered mappings, operational awards, full raw
category closure, other unadmitted sources, blocked conversions, public action,
host portability and target deployment gas remain outside this bounded intake.

## Three fixed native18 SE/LP custody and credit paths

`heldSeLp` contains complete `original` and raw `proof` objects. Originals
require `originalId`, `originalWallet`, `source`, positive `originalUnits`,
known `originalEth` and `originalDtf`, `evidenceId`, and
`contributionsKnown: true`. The four supported chain4663 sources are:

| Source | Fixed token | Eligible units |
| --- | --- | --- |
| W-SW | `0x999dae02d22e5fee1c4508430d5196d31d631009` | native18 weighted WETH/DTF SE shares |
| E-P | `0x923877336b14662cfb5b3a60b14e7d716d54a888` | native18 physical earlier LP |
| W-P | `0x46e068c2393e189fbc86632f67210af253a42aa8` | native18 physical weighted LP |
| E-S | `0xb7d4bb379d361ad442cddee53ea71a33957826a7` | native18 earlier SE shares |

These are not native28 W-SD, native9 receipt/SY units, ER internal shares,
NFT accounting shares, funded principal, or arbitrary ERC20s.
Preparation emits a separate `held-se-lp.json` review mirror. Configuration
quotes each complete original separately through the frozen evaluator,
without issuance or merging nonlinear inputs. The canonical wallet-independent
origin excludes all other representations and independent current/issued
history in both directions. A source cannot replace another source under the
same origin; Stage1 same-source wallet/input corrections remain idempotent.
Opaque alias reconciliation and approved historical originals remain
operational inputs, not facts established by token possession.

The existing paid owner-first ordinary bond precedes activation. Activation
permanently removes all14 administration selectors, including
`configureHeldSeLpEntitlements`; queries and `surrenderMigrationHeldSeLp`
remain. Stage1 surrender rejects before effects. Stage2 requires the
configured original wallet's actual native source allowance and control.
Both its debit and Migration's receipt must equal requested positive native18
q. Partial credit is full-precision floor(C*q/Q); exact terminal q==Q delivers
all remaining C. Reject zero credit, failed minimum/deadline, source or
funding/receiver failure atomically. Each successful surrender creates one
exactly funded same-wallet bond with its own fresh90-day principal cliff.
Transfer-away/back neither moves configured compensation nor resets it.
Source maximum allowances decrement too.

Only measured new q enters `migrationRecoveryInventory(source)`, in that
source's native18 units. Preexisting/unsolicited holdings, other held sources,
NFT rewards, ED, ER external E/internal B, WS gons, reserve/donor budgets
and new-bond backing remain separate. There is no new conversion, debit,
donation stage, successful-exit decoder, source enablement, or owner executor.
E-S/W-SW conversions remain unadmitted; E-P retains UnsupportedRoute/native NotOwner;
W-P retains ordinary NotOwner and owner-only liquidity. Custody/credit
acceptance does not accept their liquidation.

The new cumulative local rehearsal uses only loopback18571 and
`.omo-runtime/dtf-migration-held-se-lp/checkpoints`, with the existing
`/bin/zsh -lc` archive bootstrap. It retains all earlier routes and all three
real mined-before-checkpoint/fresh-process resumes. Earlier18567/18568/18569
signer gates remain; there is no public fallback.

Fixture acquisition is explicitly separate from production/operator authority.
W-SW uses an authenticated existing EOA's personal transfer. E-S uses actual
EOA holder `0xbab6a03be445094a10695772a79777407dcdc0e7` with pinned balance
2021090200239501983 native18 shares; this proves custody, not funded acquisition
or financial eligibility. See the retained pretransferred-mint qualification.
E-P/W-P use only
the separately admitted disposable-fork simulation: authenticate the existing
EOA collector owner and deployed `pullFee` routing; that owner releases a
small actual collector holding to itself, then separately donates its personal
holding to the controlled original. Both donor operations are impersonated,
not donor-key control, public consent, or a historical allocation. The
controlled original signs its own approval and surrender. Its original
ETH/DTF components are disclosed synthetic code-proof inputs, quoted by the
real evaluator. General execution and Migration gain neither an ability nor
a requirement to call the collector owner method. Actual users must already
control their eligible tokens.

## Earlier liquid ED: custody and credit, not conversion

`earlierLiquid` accepts complete known original records with the same
`originalId`, `originalWallet`, `source`, `originalUnits`, `originalEth`,
`originalDtf`, `evidenceId`, `contributionsKnown: true` and raw proof fields.
The only source is ED `0xaf0E1967c8F755c747615c5427108Bc549CA1122`,
chain4663. All Q0/Q/q are ED native18; credit C is new-DETF native9.
Neither current holdings nor another NFT purchase establishes these originals.
Unknown ETH or DTF rejects; explicitly known zero is valid. Operational
original allocations remain unapproved. Synthetic rehearsal inputs are labeled.

Stage1 owner-only loading and full replacement compute C0 with the complete
frozen original evaluator and issue nothing. The real paid owner-first bond
remains required. Activation permanently removes the ED loader together with
all existing loaders; moving WD loading to the smaller Migration allocation
facet changes no selector or authorization. Stage2 requires the recorded
original wallet's actual approved exact ED transfer, positive proportional
remaining credit, and one exactly funded fresh90-day-cliff bond.
Partial delivery is floor(C*q/Q); terminal q==Q pays all remaining C.
Transfer-back does not reset consumption. ED recovery inventory adds only
measured surrendered ED to the same native18 ledger as existing NFT rewards;

## 5. Data and arithmetic contract

### 5.1 Domains, units and immutable snapshot

Use native integer units throughout. ETH/WETH and historical DTF are 18-decimal inputs for this recovery; DETF credit is native 9-decimal units. Earlier receipts, LP shares, gons and staking weights retain source-specific units. Snapshot observations are not automatically original eligible quantities. Parse CSV/JSON quantities as integer strings, never floating point. An unknown blank value is not zero.

Identify a source by chain, deployed source contract and source kind. The NFT entitlement key includes collection and token ID. Domain-separate any commitments by chain ID, Migration proxy and snapshot identity to prevent cross-instance replay.

Snapshot storage must contain, or make immutably available, the complete evaluator inputs:

- Hook/token ordering, effective raw and buffered balances, weights and scales.
- Frozen fee and seigniorage fractions.
- Provider-rate values and source-specific nested deposit/redemption quote state where required.
- Contribution-to-pair routes and output-budget conversion state.
- Snapshot identity and capture block provenance.

A hash or timestamp alone is not an evaluator. Snapshot capture reads the configured contracts; the owner does not submit arbitrary output prices. Capture once after actual funding and before dependent configuration. Later funding is a donation, not permission to recapture or reprice. Scripts check the observed state against their intended funding transaction receipts.

### 5.2 Original-credit calculation

For each original entitlement `i`, retain original ETH/DTF components `E_i` and `D_i`.

```text
W = 10^18
p = frozen seigniorage fraction
S = frozen quote book

pairEq(a, x) = existing contribution-to-pair preview evaluated on S
boosted(a, x) = floor(pairEq(a, x) * (W + p) / W)
gross(a, x) = existing weighted hook quote evaluated on S and boosted(a, x)
U(a, x) = floor(gross(a, x) * (W - p) / W)
U(a, 0) = 0

C_i = U(ETH, E_i) + U(DTF, D_i)
```

The hook fee is inside `gross`, once:

```text
fee = floor(boosted * frozenSwapFeeWad / W)
net = boosted - fee
```

Then preserve the canonical rated-input mapping, weighted math, domain checks, output-budget conversion and rounding. Do not replace this with the bare mathematical weighted-pool formula if buffered SE legs add conversion behavior.

Quote both components on the same unchanged book. Do not mutate simulated reserves between them or between recipients. Do not count routed intermediate DTF as another contribution. Do not include the ordinary mint inventory leg, bond duration bonus, LP self-leg, old rewards or current redemption value in `C_i`.

Computing a user quote does not authorize replaying ordinary mint side effects. Only delivered migration principal is minted by the migration operation; separately authorized bootstrap, ordinary issuance and funded rewards retain distinct accounting.

### 5.4 Surrender arithmetic

For a fixed-principal NFT:

```text
P0 = verified original principal
Pc = actual already-withdrawn principal read from the old position
Pr = P0 - Pc

require P0 > 0
require 0 < Pr <= P0
creditToMint = floor(C_i * Pr / P0)
```

Read the remaining **total principal**, not just currently vested/claimable principal. Rewards do not increase `Pr`. Read authoritative state in the same protected operation that takes custody; reject inconsistent metadata and invalid amounts. Burned/nonexistent NFTs and reward-only positions fail even if configured.

After whole-NFT custody, mark the whole identity consumed. `C_i - creditToMint` is not another remaining NFT claim. A return/cancellation route is forbidden.

For partial fungible surrender against the source-defined eligible claim and frozen credit basis:

```text
Q = remaining eligible units
C = remaining prequoted credit
q = verified eligible units surrendered
require 0 < q <= Q

creditToMint = C                         when q == Q
creditToMint = floor(C * q / Q)           otherwise
Q_after = Q - q
C_after = C - creditToMint
```

Apply this arithmetic only after confirming the caller is the recorded original wallet and has the matching configured entitlement. An ordinary transfer does not move its configured credit or require a Migration ledger update. Keep rounding residue with that entitlement's remaining eligible claim; consuming the whole remainder transfers all remaining credit. Actual splitting, merging, claiming or wrapping must not create duplicate underlying claims or allow already surrendered assets to be credited again. Intermediate transfers do not need to be reconstructed.

Use full-precision `mulDiv` rather than overflowing products. A zero-credit surrender must revert before committing custody or consumption; do not create an empty bond or confiscate rounding dust. Users can surrender a larger eligible amount where available.

### 5.5 New bond and reward accounting

For each successful migration or independent compensation issuance:

```text
principal = deliveredCredit
claimedPrincipal = 0
startTimestamp = block.timestamp
duration = 90 days
unlockTime = startTimestamp + duration
```

Mint the exact principal to the parent funding path and use the child's exact pull/stake/gons attribution. Existing escrow surplus cannot substitute for this issuance.

```text
principalRemaining = principal - claimedPrincipal
principalDue = 0                          before unlockTime
principalDue = principalRemaining         at/after unlockTime

stakingValue = floor(stakingGons / currentGonsPerUnit)
require stakingValue >= principalRemaining
rewardsDue = stakingValue - principalRemaining
```

Reward payout requires finalized activation. Rejection changes no balances, gons, claim state or clocks. Successful claims debit the actual paid gons once. Preserve ordinary bond transfer authority and timestamps; transfer cannot pay Stage 1 rewards indirectly.

Use the existing funded distribution/index machinery; do not invent unfunded APY or calculate elapsed-time rewards from a marketing rate. Synchronize funding consistently around creation so earlier distributions are not attributed retroactively to a new bond.

In particular, settle existing participants in the parent before minting/staking new migration principal. Child synchronization while that parent's lock is held does not do this work. Initialize/advance the empty-system reward baseline so an elapsed epoch before the first funded position neither triggers `MissingRewardWeight` nor becomes a retroactive reward for that first position. Test both immediate and delayed first issuance.

### 5.6 Recovery accounting

For each selected legacy position and token:

```text
newlyReceived = balanceAfterClaim - balanceBeforeClaim
undonatedAfter =
    undonatedBefore
  + claimsReceived
  + conversionOutputs
  - conversionInputs
  - donations
```

Measure operation-local deltas; do not use the proxy's total balance as newly recovered proceeds. Separate tokens and units. A receipt claim and later DTF conversion are two stages of one recovery, not two recoveries.

Recovery selection is bounded and indexed by exact source/position. A failure reverts the selected transaction. Successful earlier stages remain in custody. Repeat calls may claim newly accrued assets, but not recount previously received or donated amounts.

### 8.1 Exact arithmetic examples

Use native DETF units in tests; human-readable quantities below are explanatory.

1. An original entitlement quotes to 1,000 DETF. Original principal 100 and remaining principal 40 yield 400 DETF, regardless of old rewards.
2. The same NFT with remaining principal zero reverts and leaves configuration, custody and supply unchanged.
3. Original contribution stays fixed when principal is partially withdrawn. Assert the delivered result is proportional to the original quote, not the smaller-input quote.
4. A fungible credit of 1,001 native DETF units on three eligible units yields 333 for the first unit, 334 for the next from the two-unit remainder, and 334 for the final unit. Aggregate never exceeds 1,001; whole-remainder surrender receives residue.

7. Loading 10,000 configured DETF credit changes neither supply nor staking backing. A 400-credit surrender changes migration-issued supply and its bond principal by exactly 400.
8. Two surrenders a month apart create two different NFTs and unlock dates a month apart.
9. A principal-only claim at the cliff never includes rewards; a Stage 1 reward claim reverts even if the principal cliff has passed.
10. Waiting more than an expansion epoch between reserve funding and the first bond neither reverts on zero allocation weight nor attributes that waiting period to the newly created bond. A later bond does not participate in rewards settled before its creation.
11. Stage 1 distributions preserve fee/creator reward rights and backing without delivering reward receipts to them. After activation, the recorded recipients can receive the proper accrued allocation exactly once.
12. A wallet holding an otherwise supported asset but having no matching configured entitlement reverts on surrender. Balances, custody, consumption, supply and bond IDs remain unchanged; surrender does not create a configuration.
13. An asset transferred to another wallet cannot use the original wallet's entitlement. The configured original wallet can surrender an asset it actually controls, subject to remaining eligibility and prior consumption, without proving intermediate transfers.

## 1. Outcome

Create a new Migration DETF type, reusing the existing Uniswap V4 DETF implementation wherever compatible and adding the facets and package needed for the migration behavior. Do not rewrite the DETF stack as a separate implementation. It has two distinct paths: **independent compensation allocation**, delivered as a bond without a user deposit, and **surrender-triggered migration credit**, delivered as a bond only when the user surrenders eligible legacy assets. Both paths use the same class of new bond: principal is locked for the full 90 days, and accrued bond rewards may be claimed during the lock only after activation. No new-instance reward claims are permitted during Stage 1.

The new package's `PkgArgs` supplies the initial administrative owner for each deployed proxy. Initialize that address through Crane's ERC8023 `MultiStepOwnableRepo` and expose the existing Ownable facet surface. The current proxy owner controls loading and alteration of both entitlement configurations, independent compensation issuance, activation and harvesting. The owner does not set a separate ETH or DTF contribution price. This supersedes every earlier fee-recipient-based migration administration role and keeps the functionality reusable across compatible packages.

The new instance has two stages. **Stage 1 - configuration:** ordinary new-money deposits are disabled except for the current owner's first paid ordinary bond under section 1.2, and all legacy surrender-triggered credit is disabled; the current owner may configure entitlements, fund reserves and execute independent compensation under its separate rules. **Stage 2 - active:** one owner-authorized atomic transaction enables ordinary deposits, eligible legacy surrender and reward claims while removing all entitlement configuration/amendment and discretionary compensation issuance selectors through ERC-2535 routing removal. No intermediate state may expose open deposits or surrender with configuration authority still usable. A partly surrendered migration entitlement can never be amended. The latest configured-original-wallet and missing-entitlement rules are recorded in implementation plan section 1.3.

Deposited legacy assets are retained under migration control for potential recovery of DTF over time. Surrender determines who receives migration credit and puts the asset in custody. It does not reprice the credit. Use the original verified historical ETH and DTF contribution amounts as mint inputs against a snapshot of the new reserve pool taken after recovery-fund funding. The credit is the user DETF the existing mint preview would return if that contribution had been deposited at that snapshot. For a legacy bond NFT, load its historical purchase contributions into migration credit configuration keyed by the source NFT contract and token ID; do not assume those contributions can be recovered from the NFT alone. Loading this configuration does not award a new bond: the matching legacy NFT must first be surrendered. No linear contribution-price setter, intermediate ETH-only accounting unit, or balance-compression curve is used.

The mint input is the original contribution. Previously claimed principal does not reduce it, and accrued or future old-bond rewards do not increase it. The contribution-based mint preview replaces the earlier blanket old-DETF-to-new-DETF 1:1 preference and the November 9 linear output-rate setters. The correspondence between each legacy entitlement and its eligible original contribution amounts must remain explicit.

The owner's funding plan is to use part of the proposed 90 ETH to acquire DTF, then donate DTF and ETH to the new DETF. A donation function accepting all underlying reserve-pool legs is required. Scripts are responsible for arranging funding before dependent configuration and bond issuance; funding is expected to be complete when entitlement configurations are loaded. Do not introduce independent funding-complete or entitlement-configuration finalization gates. During Stage 1, scripts may restructure remaining batches, resume interrupted work, make corrective funding transactions, and replace incorrect on-chain entitlement configurations of either type. Later DTF and harvested legacy DETF are donated rather than placed into ordinary bonds; future harvests are not a bootstrap prerequisite.

This is an explicit product exception for recovery. It must not silently turn ordinary DETF packages into permissioned arbitrary-mint products.

**Configuration is not delivered compensation.** Stage 1 is the configuration window: setters overwrite the complete configured entitlement for a recipient address or source NFT contract/token ID. They do not apply deltas, append another entitlement, or alter compensation already delivered. Repeating the same setter with the same values is idempotent. Stage 2 is the live stage: activation removes the entitlement-configuration facet's complete callable surface from the proxy through an ERC-2535 cut, so no caller can configure or amend entitlements afterward. There is no administrative mechanism in either stage to claw back, resize, reprice or otherwise alter delivered compensation.

### 1.1 Terms used throughout this document

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Independent compensation allocation | The owner's consolidated compensation allocation for a recipient address, without requiring that recipient to surrender assets. Multiple eligible compensation components for that recipient may be combined into this record; no separate arbitrary allocation ID is required. It excludes legacy holdings awaiting surrender. |
| Surrender-triggered migration credit | The credit awarded only when an eligible legacy asset is successfully surrendered into recovery custody. It goes to the surrendering owner as a new bond, not to an address merely because that address held the asset when configuration was loaded. |
| Migration credit configuration | The loaded source-specific historical contribution data and rules used to calculate surrender-triggered migration credit. For a bond NFT, identify the source contract and token ID and record the original ETH/DTF purchase contributions. Configuration alone does not issue credit or a new bond. |
| Entitlement configurations | The collective term for independent compensation allocations and migration credit configurations. Both may be loaded and altered in Stage 1; both become administratively immutable in Stage 2. |
| Issued bond / consumed credit | Actual consideration already delivered through either path, distinct from merely loading configuration. Configuration setters cannot alter this consideration or reset its consumption record. Keep actual issuance, claims and custody history separately; replaying or replacing configuration is not another payout or an adjustment to a delivered bond. |

Use "compensation allocation" only for the independent path, and "migration credit" only for the surrender-triggered path. Loading contribution data for a held NFT is not an independent compensation allocation for that NFT. If the holder transfers it before surrender, the new holder must surrender it to receive migration credit; the former holder receives no independent allocation for retaining or previously holding it.

### 2.2 Confirmed principal rule and resolved interpretations

The original interpretation IDs are retained for traceability. The November 9 subtraction rule is not the conversion input after the November 10 mint-preview decision:

- **MIG-A01 - Superseded as a conversion input:** The November 9 confirmation subtracted previously claimed principal from principal credit. MIG-D18 supersedes that as the amount rule. The mint input is the original contribution. Previously claimed principal is not subtracted from it and is not replenished as a second contribution. The same contribution still must not be paid twice through another representation.
- **MIG-A02:** Resolved by MIG-D13: surrender is when credit is delivered and custody is taken, not the incident snapshot or an earlier registration date. Surrender does not reprice the original contribution.
- **MIG-A03:** Resolved for the bond class by MIG-D09/MIG-D12: credit is a new bond in the common 90-day class. Principal and reward records remain useful for harvest reconciliation. They are not extra mint inputs.

The owner has fixed the 90-day duration, claim behavior and per-bond clock: principal remains wholly locked until 90 days after that bond is created, while accrued new-bond rewards are claimable during the lock only after activation. Reward claims before activation are prohibited. The assistant's earlier linear-principal-vesting suggestion is not adopted. Final recipient allocations, total issuance and execution order remain operational inputs, not a reason to reopen the settled bond rules.

### 2.2.1 Funded-snapshot mint preview

On November 10, the owner decided to use the existing DETF minting formula. The quote book is a snapshot of the new reserve pool after it is funded from the recovery fund. The mint input is the original contribution. The compensation amount is the new DETF that would be minted to the user if that contribution had been deposited at that snapshot.

This supersedes the November 9 linear output-rate compromise, including its two owner-restricted ETH and DTF contribution-price setters, owner-directed price adjustments, and prospective rate updates after migration begins. It also supersedes the provisional 1:1 old-DETF conversion, the pre-exploit ETH-denominated valuation approach, and any remaining-principal or accrued-reward scale applied to the contribution before the quote. No curve other than the existing mint preview, arbitrary minimum award, or automatic haircut is adopted.

Historical contributions mean the actual asset quantities from the old transactions, not a new read of a historical market price and not arbitrary amounts supplied by a caller. ETH and DTF amounts stay separate. Each is quoted against the same frozen snapshot, and the user outputs are summed. Quoting them sequentially against a book that moves is not the rule. Receipt tokens and NFTs identify entitlement to contributions; their raw balances are not themselves ETH or DTF contributions. For an ETH-funded purchase routed through an exchange that delivers DTF, count the original ETH once and do not also count the intermediate DTF.

The existing mint preview, not a reimplemented linear rate, is the calculation. For the Uniswap V4 DETF path, the payment is converted to the reserve pair amount, that amount is boosted by the seigniorage fraction, and the reserve hook quotes DETF out. The user receives the depositor leg after the live mint split. The seigniorage inventory leg is not the user's compensation. The hook's input fee is inside that preview. If the live mint gate would swap existing DETF instead of minting, compensation still uses the mint preview, not that swap fallback. The implementation plan must name the snapshot fields required to reproduce this preview, including reserve balances, weights, scales, the swap fee and the seigniorage fraction, and must use the existing preview rather than a hand-rolled substitute. Integer scaling and rounding are those of that preview.

The snapshot is taken after recovery funding and before dependent compensation issuance. It is not a live quote at surrender and not an owner-adjustable rate. Existing bonds and configured credits are not repriced if the live pool later changes. The plan specifies how the snapshot is captured and how the preview is evaluated. It must not add the retired linear setters.

### 2.3 Change from the earlier ledger policy

The later owner instruction to fully credit users **when they deposit old assets** changes the earlier policy recorded in [CUSTODY_AND_HARVEST.md](CUSTODY_AND_HARVEST.md) and [LOSS_AND_RECOVERY_LEDGER.md](LOSS_AND_RECOVERY_LEDGER.md).

For this draft, the intended distinction is:

- When the eligible holding is successfully surrendered into migration custody, award surrender-triggered migration credit using that configuration.
- Do not issue a second credit for the same entitlement merely because it was listed, transferred, wrapped, claimed into another representation, or later harvested.

Therefore, earlier sentences saying that a deposited asset can never receive new credit do not govern surrender-triggered migration credit. The ledger's held exclusions remain useful for separating independent compensation allocations from holdings awaiting surrender; they are not a permanent denial of migration credit after surrender.

The r20 decision is recorded in this PRD and noted in the recovery reports that would otherwise send a reader back to the linear rates or the unfilled ETH-loss formula. Frozen CSVs, evidence hashes and the November 8 ledger arithmetic are not rewritten. Their reconciliation into independent compensation allocations and migration credit configurations is future work.

## 4. Two-stage lifecycle and new-money gate

**Stage 1 - configuration** starts at deployment. Ordinary new-money deposits are disabled except for the owner's first paid ordinary bond under section 1.2; every legacy surrender-triggered credit route is disabled. The current owner may load or replace either entitlement configuration in bounded batches. Funding and independent compensation bond creation remain available under their existing requirements. No legacy token/NFT/claim may be accepted through surrender before activation; configuration never starts a migration bond clock.

Stage 1 is an operational configuration window expected to last minutes to hours while scripts run and configuration is verified. The operator will finish it before any compensation bond's principal lock expires. This is the stated operating workflow, not an additional on-chain deadline or automatic-activation gate. New-instance reward claims are prohibited throughout Stage 1 under MIG-R43.

**Stage 2 - active** begins only through MIG-R07's atomic activation. Ordinary new-money deposits and new-instance reward claims become available under their applicable rules, and all configuration/amendment authority for both paths is permanently removed along with discretionary compensation issuance. The owner cannot alter either entitlement configuration in Stage 2. Executing surrender-triggered migration credit against a frozen configuration and the post-funding mint snapshot, and recording actual consumption or claims, are not administrative configuration amendments.

The stage boundary is enforced by atomically removing the entitlement-configuration selectors and enabling ordinary deposits and eligible surrender. Stage 1 replacement changes configuration only and cannot alter independent compensation already delivered. No migration entitlement is partly surrendered in Stage 1. Stage 2 has no entitlement setter or restoration path. Ordinary claims, accrual and permitted transfers follow their existing rules and are not administrative corrections.

**MIG-R04 - Closed at initialization.** Every new Migration DETF starts with new-money issuance disabled. Deployment or receipt of the first migration deposit must not implicitly enable it.

**MIG-R05 - Complete route coverage.** While closed, all ordinary user routes that mint new DETF or buy an ordinary bond must reject that operation, including alternative selectors, bundles, and indirect routes exposing the same behavior. A caller cannot bypass the gate by labelling new capital as a migration.

**MIG-R06 - Activation-gated migration availability.** Every legacy token, NFT or claim surrender and its surrender-triggered credit is rejected in Stage 1 before custody, consumption, minting or bond funding. Activation opens eligible surrender against frozen configured original-wallet entitlements in the same atomic transaction that enables ordinary new-money deposits and removes configuration authority. Stage 2 surrender retains its recovery exception and remains subject to normal source, ownership, registry and funding checks.

**MIG-R07 - Atomic one-way enabling and loader removal.** Moving from Stage 1 to Stage 2 requires an explicit action authorized by the current proxy owner and a completed owner-paid first ordinary bond under section 1.2. That action atomically enables ordinary deposits and eligible legacy surrender and removes all configuration/amendment selectors for both entitlement types and all discretionary compensation issuance selectors as specified in MIG-R27. None of these effects may succeed alone. Activation and finalization state must be observable. There is no separate new-money closing function after activation. Normal Vault Registry disablement remains applicable without reversing activation or restoring either configuration authority.

**MIG-R43 - Reward claims require activation.** Before successful activation, reject all routes that pay rewards from the new Migration DETF, including reward claims for bonds issued through either compensation path and any alternate claim, exit or settlement route that would pay the same rewards. Neither the current owner nor another caller may bypass this requirement. A rejected reward claim leaves balances and claim accounting unchanged. Use the same finalized activation state as MIG-R07, not a separately configurable reward-opening switch; no callback during activation may claim rewards through an intermediate state.

After activation, accrued rewards may be claimed during the remaining principal lock under MIG-R23 and normal ownership, accounting and registry checks. Activation does not restart accrual, discard already accrued rewards, backdate participation or change a bond's lock. This restriction concerns payouts from the new instance; it does not prohibit authorized harvesting of surrendered legacy positions into recovery custody under section 7.

**MIG-R34 - Resumable, replaceable Stage 1 entitlement configurations.** Allow the current proxy owner to load and alter both independent compensation allocations and migration credit configurations in bounded batches throughout Stage 1, independently of the funding batch process. Repeating identical values is idempotent; corrected values replace the prior configuration rather than append another allocation or require the script to calculate a delta.

Support both reasons for amendment: restructuring unexecuted batches after a script problem, and correcting erroneous configurations already recorded on-chain. A processed configuration batch does not mean compensation has been delivered. The plan must preserve separate configuration and execution records so subsequent execution uses the applicable configuration without replaying already consumed entitlement. It must not design an adjustment mechanism for delivered compensation or treat such a mechanism as an unanswered product question. At activation, remove every loader and amendment route for both configurations, including replacement, increase, decrease, clearing and equivalent dataset/root replacement or authorization routes if such mechanisms are selected. Remaining principal and accrued rewards do not reprice that frozen credit. The exact storage representation and resumable-script checkpoints remain implementation details.

The word "premint" establishes the issuance exception. The completed allocation process must provide the recipient's compensation bond without requiring legacy-asset surrender. Initial reserve funding must precede compensation-bond creation. Within that constraint, the exact sequence of recording, minting, bond funding and receipt/ownership delivery remains an implementation-planning decision. Merely recording an allocation does not prove that the recipient has a funded bond or start its lock or reward participation.

The relationship between the paths is decided: independent compensation allocations require no deposit; surrender-triggered migration credit requires surrender.
